sources.entry: Lemma - PDF reader for mathematics textbooks and papers that turns theorem and equation references into links, folds proofs and checks the derivations you write. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/fus3r/lemma) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Lemma is a free, open-source macOS PDF reader for mathematics, statistics and computer science texts that turns references into links, folds proofs, and checks derivations you write in LaTeX.
summary.what_it_does: Lemma opens math, statistics and CS PDFs and makes references such as "Theorem 2.3", "(3.44)", "Figure 5" and "[12]" into links that can be previewed or peeked at in place, with a Back shortcut to return. It builds an outline of definitions, theorems and proofs, lets you fold proofs to attempt them first, and shows what each result uses and what uses it. A proof debugger steps over, into and out of cited results with the statement and symbols in scope. A derivation checker tests each LaTeX line you write against random values of scalars, vectors and matrices, reporting counterexamples for wrong steps. It also supports notes, highlights, spaced-repetition recall, Python notebooks, OCR, and exports to Markdown, Anki, Jupyter and annotated PDF.
use_cases: reading a math textbook with linked theorem references
stepping through a proof line by line
checking algebra steps in a derivation
studying definitions and theorems with spaced recall
exporting notes from a textbook to Anki or Jupyter
asking an AI assistant questions about a passage with its cited equations
how_to_run: Download Lemma.dmg from the project's releases and drag Lemma into Applications
Because the build is not notarized, click Done on the warning, then use System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway (once)
Or build from source: git clone the repository, cd lemma
Requires macOS 15 and Xcode 16 or later for building from source
notable: Cross-references like theorems, equations, figures and citations become hover-previewable, peekable links
Proof debugger with step over, step into and step out, plus the statement being proved shown alongside
Derivation checker that tests LaTeX steps with random values and names likely error types such as sign error or transposed
No account, analytics or tracking; network use only on explicit user actions
VS Code-style workbench with Lemma themes and support for installed VS Code themes, or a classic Mac window
caveats: macOS only, requires macOS 15 or later
Not yet notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper must be bypassed on first launch
AI assistant features need ChatGPT/Codex/Claude Code or your own API key
